who: Carol Cornwall Madsen, historian of women and American history at Brigham Young University, PhD University of Utah.

evidence.says: Her CV lists a PhD in American History from Utah (1985), BYU associate professor of history in 1986–1994, and professor in 1994–2002, covering the 1999 student record.
The authority identifies Carol Cornwall Madsen as professor of history at Brigham Young University, citing a 1995 publication.

notes: Institution, period and doctoral university agree. The CV dates the PhD to 1985; a later BYU interview says 1986. This does not affect the identity match.

who: Andrew Rippin, professor of Islamic history at the University of Victoria and scholar of Quranic interpretation.

evidence.says: The indexed supervisory committee page of Wesley Arnold Thiessen’s The Formation of the Mudawwana names Dr. Andrew Rippin, Department of History, as supervisor.
The authority identifies Rippin as University of Victoria professor of history, dean of humanities, and professor emeritus since 2013, specializing in Quranic and tafsir studies.
Victoria describes Rippin as a professor of History and researcher on Islamic history and Quranic studies.

notes: Direct student-supervisor evidence agrees with the LC candidate. The thesis committee passage was available in the search index; the full PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit.

who: Eric L. Mills, historian of science and oceanography at Dalhousie University and University of King’s College, PhD biology, Yale 1964.

evidence.says: King’s faculty biography identifies Eric Mills as Dalhousie professor emeritus of history of science; he taught and researched full time at Dalhousie and King’s in 1967–2002 and part time thereafter. His research includes nineteenth-century natural history and Canadian science.

The authority links Eric L. Mills to Dalhousie’s Department of Oceanography through Biological Oceanography (1989), and to the same history-of-science and King’s appointments through Audubon in Nova Scotia (2018).

notes: The institution, period and history-of-science field fit Shipley’s Logan dissertation. LC explicitly supplies Eric Mills as a variant of Eric L. Mills. Other candidates concern food allergy, educational administration, Chesapeake Bay writing, kinesiology or census administration; no direct Shipley supervision passage was located.

who: Neal Riemer, professor of political philosophy at Drew University, PhD government, Harvard 1947.

evidence.says: Drew identifies Riemer as Andrew V. Stout Professor of Political Philosophy, teaching there in 1972–1992, with a Harvard PhD in government (1947); his teaching included prophetic politics.
The authority links Neal Riemer to Drew through Political Science (1983) and confirms the 1972–1992 professorship and Harvard doctorate.

notes: The Drew appointment covers Rogers’s 1992 dissertation, and prophetic politics fits its subject. No direct Rogers supervision passage was located.

who: Frederick George (Fred) Stambrook, historian of European diplomacy at the University of Manitoba, PhD international history, London School of Economics.

evidence.says: The Manitoba Historical Society identifies Frederick George “Fred” Stambrook as a historian appointed to Manitoba in 1968, vice-president academic through 1991, and interim departmental head in 1995–1997 and 1998–1999; his doctorate was in international history.

The authority identifies Fred Stambrook, editor of A Sharing of Diversities (1999), as a Manitoba history professor and author of European Nationalism in the Nineteenth Century; it records Frederick George Stambrook and F. G. Stambrook as earlier heading/usage.

notes: The authority explicitly connects Fred with Frederick George. Manitoba affiliation and the European-nationalism field agree with the 1993 student record; no direct Mayer supervision passage was located.

who: Annie Bunting, York University professor of Law and Society researching forced marriage, slavery and human rights.

evidence.says: York’s repository names Bunting, Annie as advisor of Karlee Anne Sapoznik’s exact dissertation title, identifies the degree as a History PhD, and gives a 2015 copyright date.
The authority identifies Annie Bunting, co-editor of Marriage by Force? (2016), as associate professor in York’s Law and Society program.
York’s faculty profile confirms the Law and Society appointment, forced-marriage research, and co-editorship of Marriage by Force?.

notes: Exact dissertation-advisor match. A. H. (Arthur Hugh) Bunting is a separate authority associated with Change in Agriculture.

who: Maud Ellmann, University of Chicago professor of English specializing in modernism and Irish literature.

evidence.says: Her CV lists Chicago employment from 2010 and identifies her as PhD co-director of Aidan Beatty’s History dissertation, The Life That God Desires: Masculinity and Power in Irish Nationalism, 1884–1938.

The authority identifies Maud Ellmann as Chicago professor of the development of the novel in English, citing The Cambridge Companion to the Body in Literature (2015), and confirms Chicago employment from 2010.

notes: Exact student, title and co-supervision match. Her CV dates Beatty’s completion to 2014, versus 2015 in the supplied AHA record.

who: Tom Gunning, University of Chicago professor of cinema and media studies and art history, specializing in film history.

evidence.says: Chicago identifies Gunning as professor emeritus in Cinema and Media Studies and Art History, retired in autumn 2018; his work includes D. W. Griffith and the Origins of American Narrative Film.
Chicago Press identifies the same film scholar and says he taught at Chicago for over two decades.
The authority links Tom Gunning, author of D. W. Griffith and the Origins of American Narrative Film, to Chicago’s Cinema and Media Studies and Art History departments.
The other Tom Gunning authority identifies a writer and teacher associated with Loreto Secondary School and the Parable Garden Education Project in Wexford, with works including A Sacramental People.

notes: The film scholar’s institution, teaching period and field fit Gooptu’s 2009 cinema dissertation. The Wexford writer and the Thomas G. and Thomas Brian Gunning authorities are distinct candidates; no direct Gooptu supervision passage was used.
